event.summary: Environment lifecycle buttons can dispatch the opposite rendered action
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: A queued click on Suspend can resume or start the environment after a host-state refresh, and a queued Resume click can request Suspend. The action is chosen from the newest host phase rather than from the button the user saw. Details: this patch adds stopped containers to the Resume projection (sandbox_sessions.rs:230-237) and wires their rendered controls through the existing start callback. Both the header's onclick at 346 and the sidebar adapter at list/row.rs:2790 send only false for an ordinary lifecycle action. start is use_callback (274), and Operation::requested(stop, suspended) runs inside its current closure (286); Resume immediately dispatches at 287-289. Cargo.lock pins dioxus-hooks 0.7.10, whose src/use_callback.rs:8-27 replaces the inner closure every render while preserving its handle. Thus a refresh from a running state to Suspended or Stopped(waiting_for_place:false) before handling a previously drawn Suspend input changes the selected endpoint to /resume (Operation::execute at 192-196); the reverse refresh can select /suspend and may skip a question when suspend_asks finds no working activity. The container adapter calls the same host /resume provider operation (environment/podman.rs:1286-1291). This is source analysis, not an observed runtime result. SPEC_impl.md:1068-1071: 'A handler for something the user answered or confirmed acts on what the render that drew the control showed, never on state it reads when it runs.' The Operation enum's comment and existing helper-level test cover phase changes after direction capture; they do not bind direction at the rendered button. Fix: pass the render's Operation (and relevant captured consent) through ControlButtons/start, retaining current-state reads only for refusal/exclusion, and bind confirmations with the specified token mechanism. Suggested bucket: high, because lifecycle input can perform the opposite operation, including unpausing/restarting an environment the user meant to freeze. Confidence: confirmed from application and pinned framework source. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; established effect is unintended lifecycle mutation. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; no queue/coverage metadata inspected. Caveat: the same callback shape already existed for Tensorlake; this patch exposes it to stopped-container start and container pause/resume. event.summary: Ordinary Add retains source exclusion during post-Running SSH readiness
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: An ordinary new Tensorlake host whose sandbox has reached Running can keep other launches and snapshot publication for the same recipe waiting while its SSH gateway becomes ready. This is extra serialization across transport readiness, not established permanent deadlock or data loss. Details: the assigned create_recorded extraction now awaits backend.wait_tensorlake_ssh after observing Running and dropping its guard argument (hosts.rs:471-497). Ordinary Add's create_host_sandbox passes None for that argument (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:1599-1616), while its real source_guard remains in the caller: acquired at 1352/1360, held through the helper await at 1378-1380, released only at 1385. At the immediate parent revision, the outer guard was dropped at tensorlake_add.rs:1069 BEFORE the separate SSH readiness await at 1074; this is an introduced extraction-order regression, not a pre-range lock policy. Session launch transfers its real guard into PreparedSandbox/create and therefore releases it at Running as intended. The readiness backend only runs bounded/paced transport checks (provisioning/tensorlake_backend.rs:58-89); it takes no recipe source lock, so there is no source-established recursive-lock cycle. Readiness's nominal minute retry budget can be extended by its last bounded shell attempt/cleanup; no exact wall-clock duration or occurrence is claimed. Competing source selection takes lock_snapshot_use (tensorlake/hosts.rs:227); publication also needs it as supplied g045/l1 documents.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md Tensorlake prepared snapshots: 'One per-recipe async mutex excludes source selection/create through the first observed Running state from snapshot publication and deletion. Installation and supervisor attachment run outside that exclusion.' Transfer the caller's source guard into create_recorded or keep ordinary Add's readiness await after the real outer guard is dropped. Full assigned range check: only 222bf6253bcd168db04bcbb1df20180c88306998 later touches provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs; no later tensorlake/hosts.rs change is listed. This record is source analysis, not executed behavior.

Documentation check is separate: hosts.rs:360-363 says the passed guard ends at Running before the readiness helper; the implementation does drop THAT parameter at 484. The added comment accurately describes the provider/session transfer and parameter lifetime but does not account for ordinary Add's still-owned outer guard. The caller's retained 'Running is the live-process exclusion boundary' comment at 1382-1385 is now false as an effective boundary for Add. No distinct new documentation defect requiring a separate fix from this lock-transfer issue is asserted; correcting ordinary Add's ownership repairs the discrepancy. Production's lack of deadlock does not dispose of bounded delay or incorrect effective-boundary explanation.

Suggested bucket: other for unnecessary launch/build delay and possible longer billed-builder lifetime; could-be-highest: no for this established route. Preserve original f4 possible-highest ownership suspicion: accidental adoption/later deletion of an unrelated sandbox remains source-refuted by saved-ID/pending ownership checks; that original consequence is not silently erased or used to inflate this delay finding. Confidence: confirmed source/contract regression; no runtime tests or reproductions. proposed_drop: false for the bounded exclusion regression. possible_cover: confirmed duplicate of supplied g045/l1, same underlying outer-guard/helper-order defect and fix; parent owns deduplication. This is not a newly discovered independent issue in discovery, since the neighbour record was read before the source check. Revision reason: earlier candidate only refuted ownership/data-loss/deadlock routes and improperly left the independently valid bounded-delay caveat unreported. Lead f4 is closed by this finding; no unresolved premise remains for the lock ordering.
